annotation.kind: source reselection and reconstruction of the scaled input-rounding and input-underflow error bound in equation (3.13)

assumptions: The inner-product length n is positive and the finite vectors x and y have positive explicit maximum norms, so the quotients in (3.4a)-(3.4b) are defined.

The input and accumulation formats form a Model-1 binary-format family: accumulation precision and exponent range contain the input format, and the rounding maps satisfy (2.3)-(2.4), including mutually exclusive relative and underflow errors, on operations without overflow.
The scaling threshold is theta=min(fmax,sqrt(Fmax/n)) from (3.2), with fmax and Fmax derived from the two Model-1 formats.
The positive factors lambda and mu are powers of two satisfying the maximal intervals (3.4a)-(3.4b).
The computed quantity at this stage is exactly lambda^-1 mu^-1 fl(lambda x)^T fl(mu y), using componentwise input-format conversions only; accumulation-format arithmetic begins after equation (3.15).
NaNs and infinities are outside the finite-real model; the represented operations exclude overflow while retaining the paper's input-underflow terms.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P20 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p20_t2_scaled_input_error {n : Nat} {iota : Type*} (model : P20Model1 iota) (t : iota) (x y : Fin n -> Real) (lambda mu : Real) (hn : 0 < n) (hx : 0 < p20InfNormVec x) (hy : 0 < p20InfNormVec y) (hlambda : p20MaximalPowerTwoScale (p20ModelScalingThreshold n model t) (p20InfNormVec x) lambda) (hmu : p20MaximalPowerTwoScale (p20ModelScalingThreshold n model t) (p20InfNormVec y) mu) : abs (p20InputStageError model t lambda mu x y) <= p20InputStageErrorEnvelope (p20InputUnitRoundoff model t) (p20InputUnderflowEnvelope model t) (p20ModelScalingThreshold n model t) x y
formal_statement.plain_language: For the paper's maximally power-of-two-scaled row and column, the error introduced by the two componentwise input-format conversions satisfies the complete rounding-plus-underflow bound (3.13).

informal_proof: Use the Model-1 input-rounding equation to bound each inverse-scaled component error by u times the exact component plus twice theta inverse times gmin times the corresponding infinity norm. Expand the product of the two perturbed vectors, compose the left- and right-input error contractions, bound component sums by n times the infinity norms, and collect the coefficients to obtain exactly (3.13).
informal_statement: Equation (3.13): the complete exact bound for epsilon_1, the error caused by componentwise input conversion and input underflow in the scaled inner product (3.3), before accumulation-format rounding.
